root_idea.summary: A semantic field centered on securing a place or position, extending to establishment, enabled access, mastery, firmness, authority, and rank.
root_idea.development: The evidence connects concrete notions such as settled places, bird nests, and lizard eggs with derived meanings of establishing someone securely, making something attainable, becoming firmly positioned, and possessing standing or power. This describes the root's semantic orientation, not a meaning shared by every derivative.

senses.definition: To establish or settle someone securely in a place, condition, or sphere; to give a firm position.
senses.usage_conditions: Frequently used with فِي or لِ constructions for establishing someone in the land, a realm, or an appointed sphere. The Quranic use emphasizes secure establishment and standing; broader direct-object senses of granting mastery are listed separately under Classical Arabic meanings.

senses.definition: To enable someone to reach, obtain, or have power over something; to make it possible or accessible.
senses.usage_conditions: The construction أَمْكَنَهُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ places the thing within someone's power or reach. It can also describe an opportunity becoming available for attainment or capture.

senses.definition: Firmly established, fixed, or secure in a place or position.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of a settled location or secure position, as in قَرَارٍ مَكِينٍ, and may describe something securely situated or established.

senses.definition: Firmly established in standing, authority, or rank; of assured status.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of a person or being whose position and standing are securely established, including the Quranic description of one possessing rank with the Lord of the Throne.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give someone mastery, authority, or power over a thing; to put it within their power.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Typically constructed with مِنْ. This is the broader direct-object sense of the Form II verb, distinct from the Quranic establishment-in-a-place construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a euphemistic sexual construction, to grant access or allow intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in expressions addressed to a woman or describing her granting attainment; the illustrative wording does not establish a general gender restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To settle, become fixed, or become established; of a person, to become firmly established, especially in authority.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person or thing becoming steady in its place or position.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become possessed of mastery, authority, or power over something or someone; to become able to avail oneself of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Constructed with مِنْ for mastery or effective access to a thing or person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become firm; of a plant, to take firm root.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plant-related use describes firm rooting.
A noun denoting the capacity or strength to act.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state of being established or settled; a settled place or resting place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the plural, it can denote people's settled places and, in the bird-related usage, nests or resting places.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or locus containing a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The root-focused lexical discussion records this usage while also reporting a derivational debate connecting the word with ك و ن.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Greatness, high rank, or honored standing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Denotes an elevated position in the estimation of a ruler or other authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Firmly or securely settled in posture, especially seated in a stable position.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression جَلَسَ مُتَمَكِّنًا, describing a firm seated posture such as sitting cross-legged.
A concrete noun preserved in the older lexical vocabulary.

cautions: The QAC Form II lemma candidate مَكَّ is normalized to the dictionary citation form مَكَّنَ.

مَكَانٌ is included because it is explicitly discussed in the root-focused lexical evidence, although no corresponding QAC form group is supplied and its derivational connection with this root is reported as debated.

The Mufradat discussion mentions the Quranic phrase بَيْضٌ مَكْنُونٌ, but no matching QAC form group is supplied for that expression; it is therefore not presented as a separate Quranic form of this root.
